submitted.rationale: Index 22 (Bi 0.36, Cu 0.18, V 0.46) had the highest measured photocurrent, 26.5 uA. That is about twice index 60 (12.6 uA, Bi 0.40, Cu 0.17, V 0.43). The Bi-rich, V-poor index 124 gave zero. The results point to a BiVO4-like, low-Cu phase with a slight V excess as the active photoanode. MEGNet gaps agree: Bi2O3 at 2.34 eV absorbs visible light, V2O5 at 2.83 eV sits at the edge of the 2.72 eV photon energy, and CuO at 0.32 eV is narrow-gap and unsuitable.

rejected.reason: Measured zero photocurrent. The Bi-rich, Cu-containing, V-poor region (like the p-type CuBi2O4) is not photoanodic.
Measured 12.6 uA, below index 22. Being closer to Bi:V = 1 with less V excess did not help.
The CuO MEGNet gap is 0.32 eV and Cu-rich phases are p-type or narrow-gap, so they are unlikely to work as photoanodes. No budget was spent there.

consultations.verdict: Weakly uninformative-to-supportive. The MEGNet HSE gap for V2O5 is 2.83 eV, which is near or above the 2.72 eV photon energy, so V-only phases absorb poorly at 455 nm. The most promising absorber is BiVO4 (about 2.4-2.5 eV) with a small amount of Cu. Index 60 (Bi 0.40, Cu 0.17, V 0.43) is the candidate closest to Bi:V = 1:1 with the least Cu, so it is measured first.

Supportive. The MEGNet HSE gap for Bi2O3 is 2.34 eV, below the 2.72 eV photon energy. So the Bi-rich corner (Bi2O3/BiVO4 with some CuBi2O4, all with visible-light gaps) should absorb at 455 nm. Measuring index 124 (Bi 0.63) explores the second, V-poor half of the library.

Against Cu-rich compositions. The MEGNet HSE gap for CuO is 0.32 eV, so Cu-rich phases are narrow-gap, recombination-prone and not photoanodic; index 124 gave zero photocurrent. So the best choice is to stay in the BiVO4-like, low-Cu region where index 60 gave 12.6 uA. Index 22 (Bi 0.36, Cu 0.18, V 0.46) sits next to 60 with slight V excess, which usually favors monoclinic BiVO4.
